guardian.title: Spain to introduce temporary border checks on visitors from Italy
guardian.description:
Move comes in response to Rome imposing similar measures after mass migration rush to Ceuta

Spain has announced it will introduce temporary border checks on visitors from Italy in response to Rome imposing similar measures after a mass rush of people from Morocco into Ceuta.

The checks, which come “amid the persistent irregular migration pressure” facing Italy, will start at midnight on Saturday and last until 7 September, Spain’s interior ministry said in a statement.

The virus causing a massive outbreak of Ebola in the Democratic Republic of the Congo could be mutating, health officials fear, as confirmed cases pass 4,000.

Africa’s public health watchdog said the time for incremental action was over as they announced plans to scale up every aspect of the response and go “door to door” looking for patients.

guardian.description:
Observatory says 36.9C posted on Sunday is city’s highest official temperature since its records began 142 years ago, with storm driving intense heat in region

Hong Kong has officially recorded its highest ever temperature as Typhoon Dolphin swept warm air over the city, the meteorological service said.

The city’s weather observatory posted a temperature of 36.9C on Sunday, the highest recorded since records began in 1884, the Hong Kong Observatory said in the afternoon.

The storm has already swept through Japan’s southern Okinawa prefecture, injuring six people and cutting power to more than 50,000 buildings.

rfi.title: The EU has new anti-Beijing instruments, but will China have to face the music?

Beschäftigung: Mindestlohnbetrug erzeugt laut Studie 64 Milliarden Euro Schaden

Bahn-Pünktlichkeit: Fahrgastverband Pro Bahn fordert strengere Ziele für die Bahn
zeit.description: Die Bonuszahlungen für Bahnmanager sollen künftig an konkrete Ziele gekoppelt werden. Der Fahrgastverband Pro Bahn fordert etwa, die Pünktlichkeit strenger zu definieren.

Krisengebiete: 350 humanitäre Helfer starben im vergangenen Jahr im Einsatz
zeit.description: Das Völkerrecht schützt Helfer in Krisenregionen, dennoch sind sie oft Angriffen ausgesetzt. Mehr als die Hälfte der 2025 getöteten Hilfskräfte starb im Gazastreifen.

zeit.title: Drohnenangriff auf Russland: Angriffe auf Wildberries: Der Ukrainekrieg kommt zu den Russen
zeit.description: Ukrainische Drohnen treffen Lagerhallen des Onlinehändlers Wildberries. Wie stark belastet das die russische Wirtschaft? Und: Widerstand gegen die geplante Rentenreform

zeit.description: Die Elbvertiefung am Montag – Mit einem Ausflug mit Bosse nach Amrum und einer Rückschau auf das neue Hamburger Rockfestival »Amplifire«

zeit.title: Olivenölkuchen: Appetit auf einen Aperitif? Probieren Sie doch mal diesen Kuchen!
zeit.description: Aperitifs wie Campari glänzen im Glas, aber haben Sie ihn mal im Kuchen probiert? In diesem Rezept liefert er die nötige Herbe zur Süße der pochierten Nektarinen.

france24fr.title: Tour de France Femmes : Demi Vollering remporte sa deuxième Grande Boucle
france24fr.description: Demi Vollering a remporté la dernière étape du Tour de France Femmes et conservé son maillot jaune. Elle remporte son deuxième Tour après 2023.

france24fr.title: Couronne solaire, comportement animal et humain... que peuvent nous apprendre les éclipses ? (2/4)
france24fr.description: Éclipse totale de Soleil (2/4). Le 12 août, le nord de l'Espagne sera traversé par une éclipse totale, l'un des événements astronomiques les plus attendus de la décennie en Europe. De la couronne solaire au comportement des animaux, en passant par les émotions humaines, ces phénomènes continuent de livrer aux scientifiques de précieuses informations.

france24fr.title: Moyen-Orient en direct : les Houthis lancent une attaque meurtrière contre le port de Moka, au Yémen
france24fr.description: Sept personnes, dont des militaires et des civils, ont été tuées et 30 autres blessées dimanche dans une attaque des Houthis contre la ville de Moka, située sur la côte de la mer Rouge, a déclaré l'armée du Yémen. Le détroit d'Ormuz restera verrouillé tant que Washington n'acceptera pas "toutes" les conditions posées par Téhéran, ont insisté les Gardiens de la révolution. Suivez notre direct.

france24fr.title: L'Europe de l'Ouest a connu son début d'été le plus chaud jamais enregistré
france24fr.description: Selon l'observatoire européen du changement climatique, l'Europe occidentale a connu son été le plus chaud jamais enregistré entre juin et juillet, marqué par des vagues de chaleur à répétition, une sécheresse généralisée et des incendies dévastateurs en France et en Espagne. Les océans ont également atteint des niveaux record.

france24fr.title: Incendies : 370 hectares sont partis en fumée dans la Drôme, un feu se déclare en Lozère
france24fr.description: L'incendie dans le massif du Claps, dans la Drôme, a progressé, dimanche, d'une cinquantaine d'hectares, portant désormais le total à 370 hectares brûlés. Un autre incendie s'est déclaré en Lozère, parcourant 153 hectares en quelques heures et entraînant des évacuations.

france24fr.title: Des relations dégradées entre Pretoria et Abuja après le retour des ressortissants Nigérians
france24fr.description: Nigeria et Afrique du Sud, deux puissances africaines, deux moteurs de la zone de libre-échange continentale. Mais aujourd’hui leurs relations sont au plus bas. Abuja accuse Pretoria de xénophobie et de mauvais traitements envers ses ressortissants. À Lagos et à Enugu, des rapatriés témoignent au micro de nos correspondants.

france24fr.title: Benjamin Netanyahu "rejette" le plan américain pour Gaza, accepté par le Hamas
france24fr.description: En campagne électorale, le Premier ministre israélien a réaffirmé dimanche son rejet du dernier plan en 15 points de Donald Trump pour Gaza, alors même que l'armée israélienne a, de fait, suspendu ses attaques dans le territoire. Son armée "n'effectuera aucun retrait tant que le Hamas ne sera pas véritablement désarmé", a déclaré Benjamin Netanyahu.

france24fr.title: 🔴 La Néerlandaise Demi Vollering remporte le Tour de France femmes et s'offre un deuxième sacre
Tour de France femmes : la Néerlandaise Demi Vollering s'offre une deuxième Grande Boucle
france24fr.description: Après une victoire en 2023, la Néerlandaise Demi Vollering a remporté dimanche son deuxième Tour de France femmes, devançant la Polonaise Kasia Niewiadoma au classement général. Elle était arrivée en deuxième position en 2025.

france24fr.title: La Syrie annonce un accord sur le sort des bases russes situées sur la côte méditerranéenne
france24fr.description: Fruit d'un an et demi de négociations, un accord a été trouvé entre Damas et Moscou sur l'avenir de deux bases russes sur le territoire syrien, a annoncé le ministère syrien des Affaires étrangères dimanche. Les installations militaires du port de Tartous et de l'aéroport de Hmeimim, situées sur la côte méditerranéenne, seront transformées "en centres conjoints de formation".

france24fr.title: Météo-France place vingt-deux départements en vigilance orange canicule lundi
france24fr.description: Météo-France a placé, dimanche, 22 départements du centre et du sud-est du pays en vigilance orange "canicule", dont neuf nouveaux par rapport à dimanche. Un nouvel épisode caniculaire pourrait "s'étendre à de nombreuses régions de France", estime un prévisionniste.

france24fr.title: Selon Volodymyr Zelensky, jusqu'à 50 000 soldats nord-coréens ont été déployés en Russie
france24fr.description: Le président ukrainien Volodymyr Zelensky estime entre 30 000 et 50 000 le nombre de soldats nord-coréens déployés pour combattre aux côtés de la Russie, alliée de Pyongyang. Face à ce partenariat, il a exhorté Séoul à renforcer sa coopération avec Kiev, et notamment pour des systèmes de défense aérienne.

france24fr.title: Moyen-Orient : Tel Aviv "rejette" le plan américain accepté par le Hamas
france24fr.description: Noga Tarnopolsky, correspondant France 24, décrypte la situation.

france24fr.title: Moyen-Orient : Téhéran pose ses conditions sur le détroit d'Ormuz
france24fr.description: Bruno Daroux, chroniqueur international France 24, analyse la situation.

france24fr.title: Affaire des élèves disparus au Mexique : un ancien gouverneur arrêté
france24fr.description: Un ancien gouverneur accusé d'avoir dissimulé des preuves dans l'affaire des 43 étudiants disparus en 2014, qui a secoué le Mexique et reste non résolue, a été arrêté, a annoncé jeudi le bureau du procureur général. Les étudiants de l'école normale d'Ayotzinapa ont disparu le 26 septembre 2014 dans l'Etat de Guerrero (sud), alors qu'ils se rendaient en autocar à Mexico pour participer à une manifestation.

france24fr.title: Rebecca Enonchong, entrepreneuse camerounaise dans les hautes sphères du commerce mondial (1/3)
france24fr.description: Innovation africaine (1/3). Pionnière de la tech en Afrique, entrepreneuse aux multiples casquettes, Rebecca Enonchong a été nommée en juin vice-présidente de la Chambre de commerce internationale, une première pour une femme africaine. Portrait d'une "success woman" boulimique de travail, réputée pour ses prises de position tranchées tant dans le monde des  affaires qu'en politique.

france24fr.title: Incendies dans le monde, fusillade en Thaïlande, guerre au Moyen-Orient : la semaine en images
france24fr.description: Retour sur les temps forts de l'actualité de la semaine et les images les plus spectaculaires : les incendies persistent en Europe et en Amérique, bien que la majorité des feux de forêt en France soient stabilisés, une fusillade est survenue dans une école en Thaïlande faisant plusieurs morts, et la guerre se poursuit au Moyen-Orient.

france24fr.title: Foot : la Fifa dénonce "un effort concerté et continu" pour affaiblir Infantino
france24fr.description: La Fédération internationale de football a dénoncé "un effort concerté et continu de certains pour affaiblir la Fifa et son président" Gianni Infantino, samedi dans un communiqué. nzz.description: Der legitime Wunsch, ein Kind zu bekommen, kann nicht in ein Recht auf ein Kind umgewandelt werden. Weshalb Leihmutterschaft aus Sicht der katholischen Kirche die menschliche Würde verletzt.

nzz.description: Andreas Pautz forscht am Paul-Scherrer-Institut zur Kernenergie. Er hält neue Kernkraftwerke für eine sinnvolle Ergänzung zu Solar- und Windenergie. Zwei neue Reaktoren würden ausreichen, damit die Schweiz in Zukunft genügend Strom habe.

nzz.description: Während ukrainische Drohnen schwere Schäden an Russlands Energieversorgung und Militärlogistik anrichten, erhöht das Regime in Moskau offenbar den hybriden Druck auf die Unterstützer im Westen. Vorfälle wie in Leipzig könnten Teil einer neuen Offensive sein.

nzz.description: Mit dem Anschlag auf den Berliner CSD stellt sich auch die Frage nach dem Schwulenhass im Islam. Denn das Erstarken des fundamentalistischen Islams bedroht queere Menschen zunehmend auch dort, wo traditionell Liberalität praktiziert wurde.

nzz.description: Der Basistarif von knapp 30 000 Franken macht aus dem Atto 2 DM-i eines der günstigsten Plug-in-Hybrid-Modelle überhaupt auf dem Schweizer Markt.

nzz.title: Die EU setzt in der Migrationspolitik auf nordafrikanische Staaten – doch auch dort will man die Migranten nicht
nzz.description: Libyen kommt eine Schlüsselrolle in der europäischen Migrationspolitik zu. Doch in der libyschen Bevölkerung wächst der Unmut über illegal Eingereiste, die möglicherweise gar nie nach Europa migrieren.

nzz.title: Pannenserie bei Liechtensteiner Staatsbauten: Die Steuerzahler müssen die Fehlplanungen bezahlen

nzz.title: Essen die Amerikaner bald deutsche Burger? Eine Berliner Fast-Food-Kette träumt vom grossen Geschäft in den USA

nzz.title: GASTKOMMENTAR - Familienmediation beruht auf Freiwilligkeit und Vertraulichkeit
nzz.description: Mediation, Elternberatung und Therapie werden oft vermischt oder gleichgesetzt. Ein Mediationsverfahren aber ist stets freiwillig, es kann lediglich ein Mediationsversuch angeordnet werden. Gerade im Zusammenhang mit häuslicher Gewalt ist dies zentral.

nzz.title: Über Jahrzehnte sickert bei einer chemischen Reinigung in Winterthur giftiges Lösungsmittel in den Boden. Wer bezahlt?
nzz.description: Das Haus ist längst abgerissen. Doch weil die Stadt darunter auf eine böse Überraschung stiess, zieht sich ein Rechtsstreit hin.

spiegel.title: New York: Boot kentert nahe Freiheitsstatue - Frau und Baby sterben
spiegel.description: Bei einem Bootsunglück nahe Liberty Island in New York sind zwei Menschen ums Leben gekommen, zwölf weitere konnten gerettet werden. Der Bootsführer wurde festgenommen und angeklagt.

spiegel.description: Nikolas Stihl betrachtet die 35-Stunden-Woche als Luxus vergangener Tage. Seine Forderungen dürften Zündstoff für die Tarifgespräche im Herbst liefern.

spiegel.title: Humanitäre Hilfe: Hunderte Helfer starben im vergangenen Jahr im Einsatz

spiegel.description: Bestechung, gefälschte Dokumente, illegale Lieferwege: Deutsche Rüstungsfirmen sorgten in der Vergangenheit immer wieder für Skandale, oft mit tödlichen Folgen.

spiegel.description: Ein 30-Jähriger ist in Berlin-Charlottenburg erschossen worden. Die Täter sind flüchtig, eine Mordkommission ermittelt.

spiegel.description: Die Interessenvertreter schlagen Alarm: Wenn Regen weiterhin ausbleibt, werden die Schiffer des Rheins sich aufteilen müssen: Die einen befahren den Nordrhein, die anderen die Region im Süden.

spiegel.title: Homeoffice und Einsamkeit: Lasst alle zu Hause!
spiegel.description: Statistiker und Arbeitgeber sagen: Homeoffice ist schädlich und macht potenziell einsam. So einfach ist die Sache nicht.

spiegel.title: Deutsch-französischer Krieg 1870/71: Die verdrängte Wahrheit über die deutsche Einigung
spiegel.description: Schnellfeuergewehre, Millionenheere, überforderte Ärzte: Der Deutsch-Französische Krieg nahm die Schrecken des Ersten Weltkriegs vorweg. Doch der Jubel über die deutsche Reichsgründung überstrahlte das Leid der Soldaten.

spiegel.title: Die Angst um den Job lähmt Sie und killt jede Ambition? So bleiben Sie motiviert
spiegel.description: Wer dachte, dass Leistung und Loyalität automatisch Job und Aufstieg sichern, erlebt nun, wie selbst exzellente Karrieren abrupt unterbrochen werden können. Wie Sie Zuversicht und Kontrolle zurückerlangen können.

spiegel.description: KI-Agenten können schneller programmieren als Softwareentwickler, und Tausende Informatiker sind plötzlich arbeitslos. Welche Fähigkeiten in der Branche jetzt gefragt sind.

spiegel.description: Der US-Präsident versucht, die jüngsten Rückschläge bei den Verhandlungen mit Teheran kleinzureden. Und aus Israel kommt eine Ansage, die Donald Trump gar nicht gefallen dürfte. Der Überblick.

spiegel.title: Daniel Kinahan zurück in Irland: Emirate liefern mutmaßlichen KOCG-Gangsterboss aus
spiegel.description: Dem Iren Daniel Kinahan wird vorgeworfen, Kopf einer europaweit agierenden kriminellen Organisation gewesen zu sein. Nun wurde der 49-Jährige aus Dubai in seine Heimat geflogen – und kam sofort vor ein Gericht.

spiegel.title: NBA: Dirk Nowitzki trauert um seinen ersten Trainer Don Nelson
spiegel.description: Der Einstand in der NBA verlief für Dirk Nowitzki im Jahr 1999 holprig. Einer seiner größten Fürsprecher: Dallas-Trainer Don Nelson. Der ist nun mit 86 Jahren gestorben. Und der deutsche Superstar verabschiedete sich mit rührenden Worten.

spiegel.title: Grünen-Abgeordneter Kassem Taher Saleh spricht erstmals öffentlich über seine Depression
spiegel.description: Eine Depression bremste den Grünenabgeordneten Kassem Taher Saleh aus. Im SPIEGEL spricht der 33-Jährige erstmals öffentlich über seine Erkrankung und darüber, was sie mit dem Politikbetrieb zu tun hat.

phys-org.title: How dogs evolved differently across the globe to match human traits
phys-org.description: We call them "man's best friend," and the evidence supports it. Dogs have been found buried alongside humans in graves dating back 14,000 years. They appear in ancient art from every continent, and they feature in the mythology, religion and folklore of virtually every culture. Archaeological evidence shows they have helped us hunt, protected our homes, hauled our possessions, herded our livestock and provided companionship through the entirety of recorded history.

phys-org.title: Controlled cracking technique prints quantum dots into tiny pixels for sharper displays
phys-org.description: Recent technological advances have enabled the development of increasingly sophisticated, sharper displays for electronic devices. Many modern displays use light-emitting diodes, or LEDs, tiny semiconductor-based components that emit light when an electrical current passes through them.

phys-org.title: Hong Kong weather observatory posts record high temperature
phys-org.description: Hong Kong's weather observatory posted a record high temperature of 36.9°C (98°F) on Sunday as Typhoon Dolphin swept warm air over the city, the meteorological service said.

phys-org.title: How to spot the Perseid meteor shower, a summer light show that promises to dazzle
phys-org.description: The Perseid summer light show is back—and viewing conditions are especially promising for the Northern Hemisphere.

phys-org.title: Early snakes explored life underground, on land and at sea
phys-org.description: Snakes are highly modified lizards, with more than 4,000 living species today. The origin of snakes has long been one of evolutionary biology's most debated questions. Their sparse fossil record has made it hard to pin down what drove the evolution of their limbless body plan.

phys-org.title: New catalyst with 75% less platinum promises to reduce the cost of hydrogen fuel cells
phys-org.description: The high cost of platinum is one of the main barriers to the wider adoption of hydrogen fuel cells. Now, researchers at IMDEA Materials Institute have developed a catalyst that delivers the same performance while using 75% less of this expensive metal. The study, published in Electrochimica Acta, demonstrates a breakthrough made possible by applying controlled mechanical compression to the catalyst. phys-org.title: Australia has pledged to restore nature. But could we ever bring back lost ecosystems?
phys-org.description: Nature is not doing well in Australia. Many unique mammals, birds and insects are struggling. Entire ecosystems are collapsing.

phys-org.title: Tiny particles defy action-reaction symmetry to stay in motion
phys-org.description: From schools of fish and flocks of birds to microscopic synthetic particles, many systems in nature and the laboratory consist of individual units or agents that move by consuming energy. These systems are known as active matter because their components continuously use energy to generate motion, either individually or through interactions with their environment.

phys-org.title: Cosmic filaments help set first limits on dark matter's decay into gravitons
phys-org.description: Composing some 85% of the universe's total mass, dark matter betrays its presence only through gravity, unlike ordinary matter. Yet through new research published in Physical Review D, a team led by David Dunsky of New York University has proposed a new way to hunt for the elusive substance. Their approach involves searching for the decay of dark matter particles into gravitons: the hypothetical particles thought to carry the force of gravity itself.

phys-org.title: Over half of people are unaware of the environmental effects of sunscreen
phys-org.description: This summer, millions of people across the country have been digging out sunscreen to protect themselves from a record-breaking series of heat waves.

phys-org.title: Rare Mars meteorite preserves 1.27-billion-year-old clues to planet's deep interior
phys-org.description: Boston College scientists have determined that a newly discovered meteorite from Mars is 1.27 billion years old and derived from a previously unsampled, pristine source on the Red Planet. The study is published in the journal Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta.

phys-org.title: Oldest known giant rock scallop bead suggests California coastal trade began millennia earlier
phys-org.description: Archaeologists have discovered two giant rock scallop beads that push back the clock on the first appearance of these high-status ornaments. The discovery shows that these prized marine beads were traded hundreds of miles from the California coast thousands of years earlier than previously thought.

phys-org.title: Charge-based strategy improves controlled delivery of therapeutic peptides from gelatin-based materials
phys-org.description: Rice University engineers have developed a new strategy for controlling how therapeutic peptides are released from gelatin-based materials, a step that could make the small but powerful molecules more useful in tissue engineering and drug delivery.

phys-org.title: The asteroid that may be three worlds
phys-org.description: What shape is an asteroid? For (44) Nysa, the honest answer until now has been that nobody knew. It is one of the brightest and largest E-type asteroids in the main belt, a class with a surface rich in enstatite, and its oddness has made it a favorite target for well over a hundred years. Successive observations hinted that it was elongated, perhaps even two lumps stuck together, but the picture stayed frustratingly blurred.

phys-org.title: 'Flying focus' laser overcomes key limitation in plasma-based particle accelerators
phys-org.description: In a new Nature Physics study, researchers accelerated electrons to more than twice the energy predicted by the traditional dephasing limit for laser-plasma accelerators operating over the same distance. This was made possible by a specially engineered laser pulse called a flying focus, which counteracts a longstanding limitation known as "dephasing."

phys-org.title: Butterfly ranges shift worldwide amid climate change, with most species expanding their reach
phys-org.description: A global analysis of range-shift records for 1,758 butterfly species—10% of known butterfly species—found that 80% had expanded their range and that 79% of all recorded range shifts were linked to climate change and extreme weather events. The new study, published in Nature Ecology & Evolution, also reports range contractions for 27% of species, and 22% of species showed a change in elevation. phys-org.title: Pulsed radiofrequency magnetic fields may disorient migratory birds, experiments suggest
phys-org.description: Every year, millions of migratory birds travel between different geographical regions on Earth to find food, escape cold weather or reach safe environments to raise chicks. To determine which direction to fly, these birds rely on various types of sensory cues and information, including the magnetic field surrounding our planet, known as the geomagnetic field.

phys-org.title: Dodo birds more clever than we thought
phys-org.description: The Mauritian dodo—a global symbol of human-caused extinction and one of the world's largest pigeons—may not have deserved its reputation as a silly simpleton and may have been the only member of its group to live in the dark.

undark.title: Book Review: How Wildlife Is Returning to the East
undark.description: In “The Beasts of the East,” journalist Andrew Moore charts the natural history of the East and the people who have dedicated their careers to restoring several long lost species to what remains of their original habitats.

undark.title: Book Review: The Case for the AI-Powered Global Brain
undark.description: In “The God Test,” Robert Wright considers a future in which human consciousness becomes infused with AI. “We have to think seriously about a future in which there is something that increasingly resembles a global brain, and its neurons increasingly consist not just of human brains but of AIs,” he writes.

undark.title: Interview: How Tragedy Changed the FDA
undark.description: As an FDA advisory committee prepares to weigh whether specialized pharmacies should be allowed to dispense seven unapproved peptides, Mikkael A. Sekeres, a scientist and former adviser, discusses the history and nuances of FDA oversight, including its process for screening advisory committee members for conflicts of interest.

undark.title: Will AI Fix Prior Authorization — or Make It Worse?
undark.description: The Trump administration is currently piloting a program in six states that expands Medicare prior authorizations using AI tools in an effort to reduce unnecessary medical spending. But it remains to be seen whether this new approach, which the administration has called “broken” in the private sector, will be effective without causing dangerous delays for Medicare recipients.

undark.title: Biologists Should Articulate Their Position on AI
undark.description: Last month, mathematics researchers released the Leiden Declaration, a treatise on how to handle the challenges that artificial intelligence poses to their field. C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that biologists should learn from the mathematics community and work on their own version.

undark.title: Review: What Animals Can Teach Humans About Caregiving
undark.description: From seahorses and birds to beetles and killer whales, journalist Elizabeth Preston finds a lot of common ground  between human and animal parenting in “The Creatures’ Guide to Caring,” a sweeping survey of the evolution of caregiving and the dizzying array of survival strategies in the animal kingdom.

undark.title: The MAHA Movement’s Worrisome Embrace of Ibogaine
undark.description: The MAHA movement has been promoting the plant-based substance ibogaine as a remedy for opioid addiction, despite the lack of clinical trials on its safety and efficacy. One physician who practices addiction medicine discusses the risks of ibogaine and argues for the need to support proven treatments.

undark.title: Advocacy Groups Express Mixed Views on Embryo Editing
undark.description: At least two new start-up companies, Preventive and Origin Genomics, say they are developing strategies that combine gene editing with in vitro fertilization to correct disease-causing mutations. Advocacy groups for people living with these genetic disorders have been quiet on the developments.

undark.title: Interview: California Lawmaker Calls for a Peptide Working Group
undark.description: Amid a national push to ease restrictions on certain peptides, California legislator Joe Patterson has introduced a state-level bill that would to establish a working group tasked with making recommendations to allow physicians and hospitals, among others, to prescribe and study promising peptides.

undark.title: Making Sense of Data From Wearable Health Trackers
undark.description: Wearable health devices such as smartwatches, glucose monitors, and sleep trackers are blurring the line between consumer wellness and clinical medicine. One physician argues that validation standards and privacy protections must be established to ensure the usefulness of the data these devices generate.

proj-syn.title: The Ceuta Crisis Is About More Than Migration

proj-syn.title: The Rising Price of a Cheap Renminbi
proj-syn.description: Renminbi appreciation would not, on its own, rebalance China’s economy and eliminate its massive surpluses. But by increasing households’ purchasing power over imports and compressing tradable-sector margins, it would raise the cost of avoiding reform.

proj-syn.title: Who Should Build the Low-Carbon Economy?
proj-syn.description: Since the first Industrial Revolution, goods and technologies have reached the farthest corners of the world, but the ability to design, build, market, and extract value from them has remained highly concentrated. Unless humanity can break this pattern, a sufficient response to climate change will remain out of reach.

proj-syn.title: Will Iceland Rejoin the EU Path?
proj-syn.description: US President Donald Trump’s volatile and unpredictable security policies, particularly his desire to control Greenland, have put Iceland in a vulnerable position. This uncomfortable reality will likely be front of mind as voters decide whether to reopen membership negotiations with the European Union.

proj-syn.title: Democracy, Autocracy, or Something Else?
proj-syn.description: Contrary to conventional wisdom, the world is neither converging on liberal democracy nor being swept by an authoritarian tide. The decisive political struggles of the 21st century will be won or lost through the unglamorous work of strengthening democratic accountability and building effective institutions.

proj-syn.title: Colombia’s New Right-Wing Government Faces an Uphill Battle
proj-syn.description: Colombian President-elect Abelardo de la Espriella inherits an economy constrained by weak investment and a severe fiscal crisis. His ability to restore fiscal stability without sacrificing the social gains of recent decades will determine whether the country’s rightward shift proves lasting or short-lived.

proj-syn.title: Can Progressives Deliver Economic Growth?
proj-syn.description: At a time of historic inequality and inadequate public investment, the kind of redistributive policies promoted by politicians on the left are badly needed. But given that no jurisdiction can tax and regulate its way to affordability, a growth-enhancing agenda that generates good jobs and productive capacity is also vital.

proj-syn.title: Fauci’s Modern Pillory
proj-syn.description: MAGA Republicans’ decision to drag Anthony Fauci before a Senate hearing was less about their hatred of science and more about their disdain for the scientists who guide lawmakers in their decision-making. They couldn’t wait to pillory him, and by association any public-facing expert, in front of the cameras.

proj-syn.title: Cheaper Mortgages Won’t Solve the US Housing Crisis
proj-syn.description: For decades, federal housing policy has favored cheaper financing over expanding the housing supply, despite evidence that expanding mortgage credit increases borrowing and house prices. The bipartisan 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act marks an important shift by emphasizing measures that make it easier to build more homes.

proj-syn.title: The Right Way to Regulate AI
proj-syn.description: Governments tend to treat AI as a national-security challenge while devoting far less attention to its effects on education, health, labor markets, and the judiciary. Addressing AI’s societal risks requires institutions designed to recognize and respond to emerging threats before they become systemic failures.

proj-syn.title: Global Tax Reform Is the Key to a Fair AI Economy
proj-syn.description: The rise of AI has highlighted how the global tax system is ill-suited to capture the profits derived from such technology. While creating an equitable AI economy ultimately requires a durable and robust multilateral tax framework, digital-service taxes can serve as an important stepping stone to that outcome.

proj-syn.title: Aid’s Next Chapter
proj-syn.description: Wars, epidemics, displacement, and geopolitical competition will ensure that rich countries continue to spend money abroad, whether for humanitarian reasons or in pursuit of their own interests. The only question is what sort of aid system will emerge from the current retrenchment.

proj-syn.title: Peace With Iran Won’t Last Unless It Benefits Ordinary Iranians
proj-syn.description: A sustainable peace agreement between the United States and Iran will require more than military deterrence. Without financial sanctions relief that fuels job creation and generates real economic opportunities for ordinary Iranians, it will likely suffer the same fate as the 2015 nuclear deal.

proj-syn.title: Why Wealth Taxes Always Fail
proj-syn.description: A clear-eyed view of past experience shows that where wealth taxes have been tried, they have usually been abandoned—and for good reason. As policymakers in California, New York, France, and elsewhere revisit this old idea, they should heed the lessons of this history.

proj-syn.title: A New Paradigm for Global Health Financing
proj-syn.description: As aid flows decline, more countries are articulating a new vision in which health financing would build on national resources, answer to domestic priorities, and remain accountable to their own citizens. Such a change is long overdue, and it can be achieved by pursuing reforms in three areas.

proj-syn.title: The Triumph of India’s Cockroaches
proj-syn.description: The concessions secured by the "cockroach movement" amount to more than a triumph for prospective medical students or a brief political headache for the country's ruling party. They prove that even after years of centralization and institutional erosion, power remains with the people.

proj-syn.title: Zombie Monetarism
proj-syn.description: Three prominent economists, including a former Federal Reserve governor and adviser to US President Donald Trump, have just endorsed “soft monetarism” as a way to guide the Fed's approach to inflation. But the "quantity theory" of money failed for good reasons, and those reasons have not changed.

proj-syn.title: Taiwan Needs a New Deterrence Strategy
proj-syn.description: Emboldened by US President Donald Trump’s war in Iran, Chinese leaders have ramped up their gray-zone coercion against Taiwan in recent months. To avert a Chinese invasion, Taiwan must ensure that other democracies cannot function without it by providing them with more than just semiconductors.
